Seven middleware modules import `HTTPException` from `src/http-exception.ts` (excluding test files):

| Middleware | File | Usage |
|---|---|---|
| **basic-auth** | `src/middleware/basic-auth/index.ts:7` | Throws `HTTPException(status, { res })` on auth failure (`:126`) |
| **bearer-auth** | `src/middleware/bearer-auth/index.ts:7` | Local `throwHTTPException` helper throws with 401 (missing/invalid token) or 400 (invalid request) (`:109`) |
| **body-limit** | `src/middleware/body-limit/index.ts:7` | Throws `HTTPException(413, { res })` when the payload exceeds the limit (`:64`) |
| **csrf** | `src/middleware/csrf/index.ts:7` | Throws `HTTPException(403, { res })` on origin mismatch (`:85`) |
| **ip-restriction** | `src/middleware/ip-restriction/index.ts:8` | `blockError(c): HTTPException` returns a 403 used as the default denial handler (`:141`) |
| **jwt** | `src/middleware/jwt/jwt.ts:8` | Throws 401 for missing/malformed header (`:70`), and for verification failures (`:106`, `:124`) |
| **timeout** | `src/middleware/timeout/index.ts:7` | Default `HTTPException(504)` (`:12`); the `exception` option accepts an `HTTPException` or an `HTTPExceptionFunction` returning one |

Only `timeout` exposes it in its public type surface — it exports `HTTPExceptionFunction = (context: Context) => HTTPException`. The others use it purely internally as the thrown error.

Test files also reference it (`timeout/index.test.ts`, `jwt/index.test.ts`), and outside `src/middleware/` it's used by `src/validator/validator.ts` and `src/adapter/cloudflare-pages/handler.ts`.
